As a Redditor, I have an inclination for seeking out controversial topics that encourage progression. I felt unsatisfied with my pursuit until I came across FatPeopleHate in May and my whole perspective on life changed. I would like to share my story that helped build this perspective.

Earlier this year, I came across Delusional Artists, which encourages the public admonishment and ridicule of individuals. I tried to concentrate on the positives of this subreddit, such as the idea that tough love can build an artist or even that it can be a lesson to not put forward products that are not professional. However, I came to the conclusion that nothing was built up and personal harm was encouraged, as their perspective on disclosure had no limits and that their ridicule only encourages people who do what they love to commit suicide. There was no incentive to preserve and maintain one's dignity, but only to destroy it.

I came across Confessions, which is built entirely upon shortcomings. Self-preservation, however, is traded up for fee-fees; everyone is a winner in their book. Their definition of "tough love" is as broad as our Solar System and denial is praised along the lines of "good morale".

Then, I found FatPeopleHate... where I realized I have always been a shitlord and where I was reminded about the pride of being a human and not a planet. If someone's image is hideous and inhuman, then it deserves to be busted. Others' failings remind us to move forward as active creatures that only stop when we die. These are values that I have always treasured and appreciated, but only with the discovery of FPH was everything put into perspective and I found a venue to vent my oppressively-caged frustrations about getting stalled and weighed down by others' shortcomings. We are a species that was made in a beautiful form and we owe it to our own existence to preserve that form... and to toughly remind the dead weight of our species why we must do this.

So, thank you all and I am happy to be with you!
